learner_facing_text: This course teaches rigging leadership and verification architecture only. It does not qualify a novice to perform overhead rigging, work at height, operate hoisting systems, make engineering decisions, inspect/sign off a rig, or receive employer/venue rigging authorization.
notes: Normalized from existing course boundary. Intentionally non-operational.

learner_facing_text: ETCP rigging certifications are aimed at experienced riggers and separate Arena and Theatre rigging into distinct certification domains based on different bodies of knowledge.
notes: Supports external-specialist gating; does not imply ETCP is the only valid qualification route.

learner_facing_text: Crew Blueprint can teach terminology, documentation, role boundaries, communication and escalation around rigging, but practical rigging competence and authority require external training, supervised experience and employer/venue qualification appropriate to the actual system and work.
notes: External-gate synthesis; not a claim that one credential or one training provider is universally mandatory.

learner_facing_text: Entertainment rigging is not one interchangeable system: current consensus standards separately address system families such as manual counterweight rigging and entertainment chain-hoist use.
notes: Scope/version fact only. Detailed standard requirements remain outside general course instruction unless separately reviewed.

learner_facing_text: Fall-protection requirements must be mapped to the actual work and applicable standard; the course does not teach climbing, fall-protection setup, rescue, or work-at-height procedure.
notes: OSHA general-industry rules include scope-specific exceptions, so the course must not present one universal entertainment-stage fall rule.
